definitions.full: H5036. nabal I. נָבָל adjective foolish, senseless , especially of the man who has no perception of ethical and religious claims, and with collateral idea of ignoble, disgraceful ; — absolute ׳נ 2Sam 3:33 14 t.; masculine plural נְבָלִים 13:13 ; Ezek 13:3 ( ᵐ5 Co מִלִּבָּם ); feminine plural נְבָלוֺת Job 2:10 ; — senseless , especially of religious and moral insensibility: נ ׳עַם Deut 32:6 (of Israel, unappreciative of J.'s benefits; opposed to חָכָם ), so of heathen nation Psa 74:18 (blaspheming name of ׳י ), נ ׳גּוֺי Deut 32:21 (|| עָם לֹא ); הַנּ ׳הַנְּבִאִים Ezek 13:3 (si vera lectio, see above); elsewhere as substantive (impious and presumptuous) fool, Isa 32:5 (opposed to נָדִיב noble-minded ), characterized as at once irreligious and churlish, 32:6 ; denying God Psa 14:1 = 53:2 ; insulting God 74:22 , and God's servant 39:9 ; Prov 17:7 arrogant speech becometh not the (impious and presumptuous) fool (whose faults it only makes the more conspicuous), much less do lying lips him that this is noble ( נדיב ), 17:21 (|| כְּסִיל ), 30:22 לחם ישׂבע כי ונבל (one of the things under which the earth trembles), נָבָל בְּנֵי Job 30:8 i.e. ignoble men (|| בְלִישֵֿׁם בְּנֵי ); as one who might be expected to have a contumelious end, נ ׳הַכְּמוֺת אבנר ימות 2Sam 3:33 was Abner (destined) to die, as a ׳נ dieth ? of the man who amasses riches unjustly נבל יהיה ובאחריתו Jer 17:11 i.e. will prove himself to be a ׳נ ; as acting immorally (with collateral idea of disgracefully) 2Sam 13:13 בישׂראל הַנְּבָלִים כְּאַחַד תהיה ואתה (compare נְבָלָה ); feminine only in הַנְּבָלוֺת אַחַת כְּדַבֵּר Job 2:10 (of Job's wife). compare Dr Deut 22:21 . 32, 6. 15.21 ; Psalt. 457.

occurrences.englishText: Is this the way you repay Yahweh,
They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God.
The king lamented for Abner, and said, “Should Abner die as a fool dies?
As for me, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from you.”
But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?”
They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men.
The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.”
God looks down from heaven on the children of men,
Remember this, that the enemy has mocked you, Yahweh.
Arise, God! Plead your own cause.
Arrogant speech isn’t fitting for a fool,
He who becomes the father of a fool grieves.
For a servant when he is king,
The fool will no longer be called noble,
For the fool will speak folly,
As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid,
The Lord Yahweh says, “Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!
